name: Software Configuration Management
one_liner: Control changes to every artefact and keep the configuration's integrity and traceability.
purpose: Developing a solution creates hundreds of artefacts — documents, code files, scripts, deliverables — that need to be managed. In PM²-Agile, Software Configuration Management provides the key activities that consistently control changes to the configuration and maintain its integrity and traceability. It has four primary objectives and a set of process steps, and its development-specific considerations are documented in alignment with the PM² Quality Management Plan.
meta: Identify items, simplify builds, maintain quality, increase productivity
Identification, Change Control, Version Control, Configuration Auditing, Reporting

items: Identify and manage all items that are part of configuration management
Simplify the build of different versions of the solution
Ensure quality is maintained as the configuration evolves
Increase productivity by reducing mistakes, through automation
Identification — uniquely identify each configuration item added to the repository
Change Control — the existing PM² process for documenting, assessing and approving changes
Version Control — procedures and tools to manage multiple occurrences of each object
Configuration Auditing — a quality assurance activity ensuring quality is maintained as changes are made
Reporting — informs anyone in the project or organisation about the changes that occurred
Assign each configuration item to a specific version of the solution
Maintain a record of each item — name, creation date, last update, version — for audit purposes
Describe naming and versioning conventions in compliance with corporate regulations
Adopt a standard product directory structure for artefacts under version control
Use synchronisation control so parallel changes do not override each other
Manage change requests including enhancements and defects from the team and external stakeholders
Physical location of servers and client machines

fields.what: Hundreds of artefacts — documents, code files, scripts, deliverables — are created during development and need to be managed.
fields.pollux: Four releases of portal code, scripts and report definitions.

fields.what: Key activities that consistently control changes to the configuration and maintain its integrity and traceability.
fields.pollux: Directly answers the audit findings on reporting version control (SC5).

fields.what: The team must identify all items they need to track — classes, libraries, test scripts, deployment files — and manage them with specific tools.
fields.pollux: Includes the report definitions that used to live in spreadsheets.

fields.what: Development is incremental, with versions regularly demonstrated and delivered, so building and delivering a specific version must be easy.
fields.pollux: Any of the four releases can be rebuilt on demand.

fields.what: As the configuration evolves, quality is maintained by tracking items, their change history and the impact of those changes.
fields.pollux: Change impact on exposure figures is traceable, not reconstructed.

fields.what: With the right tools, configuration management can be automated until human intervention is residual, reducing mistakes and raising productivity.
fields.pollux: Removes the manual version juggling behind the eleven spreadsheets.

fields.what: Uniquely identify each configuration item; an object-oriented approach helps aggregate similar objects using properties like name, version and type.
fields.pollux: Every report definition gets an identity of its own.

fields.what: Already foreseen as a PM² process defining activities related to project changes, including documenting, assessing and approving them.
fields.pollux: Reuses PM² change control rather than inventing an agile substitute.

fields.what: Procedures and tools that let an Agile Team Member collect all relevant configuration objects and build a specific version of the solution.
fields.pollux: The team can rebuild Release 1 exactly while Release 2 is in flight.

fields.what: A quality assurance activity checking that changes were highlighted, documented and authored, and that procedures were followed.
fields.pollux: Gives Internal Audit the trail it found missing twice.

fields.what: Details the change initiator, the time and date, the scope of the change and other relevant information, aligned with the Communications Management Plan.
fields.pollux: Aligned with your project-level communication plan.

fields.what: As an item moves through the process, some steps may not apply — a configuration script change may need no change request.
fields.pollux: A build script tweak does not go to change control.

fields.what: Development-specific considerations such as tools and templates should be documented in alignment with the PM² Quality Management Plan.
fields.pollux: Recorded in the Development Handbook alongside the tooling choices.

fields.what: Synchronisation control ensures parallel changes will not override each other.
fields.pollux: Matters with a distributed team including a seconded supplier.

fields.what: Analyse anticipated product data size, team distribution and the physical location of servers and client machines.
fields.pollux: Relevant with Levallois Systems staff working alongside ESM's team.

fields.what: Document how software developed by vendors and subcontractors is incorporated into version control.
fields.pollux: Eiffel's Levallois Systems code enters the same repository and rules.

traps: Not every configuration item passes every step — a script change may skip Change Control.
Configuration Auditing is a quality assurance activity, not a version-control step.
Reporting aligns with the PM² Communications Management Plan.
Change Control is an existing PM² process, reused rather than reinvented.
SCM tooling and template choices align with the PM² Quality Management Plan.
